nextStoryContext: cam issue get <id> is now a pure, deterministic, read-only CLI subcommand: src/commands/issue-get.ts exports getIssueOnMain(cwd, id, spawnFn = spawnSync), which reuses issueFilePath (src/issues/backlog.ts) for the CAM-42 -> CAM-0042.json zero-padding and BacklogSpawnFn for the injectable spawnSync type, then runs `git show main:scripts/cam/issues/<PREFIX>-NNNN.json`. Non-zero exit from git show (verified empirically: `git show main:<missing path>` exits 128, no stdout) maps to { ok: false, reason: 'not-found' }; success maps to { ok: true, id, content } with the raw stdout. Wired into index.ts: ParsedIssueArgs gained `{ mode: 'get'; id: string; help: false }`, parseIssueArgs detects `get <id>` before the free-text fallthrough (missing id or extra args are parse errors, mirroring close/abandon/demote), IssueDispatchDeps gained an optional `getIssueOnMainFn` injection point, dispatchIssue's `mode === 'get'` branch prints the raw JSON to stdout on success (exit 0, deliberately no CAM_ISSUE_RESULT machine line since that contract is scoped to mutation outcomes) and a clear error to stderr on failure (exit 1), and ISSUE_HELP got a `get <id>` Arguments entry plus a usage-string update. Read-only: no CAS, no commit, no working-tree write -- contrast with close/abandon/demote (US-002/US-003 sibling work per prior notes) which do mutate/commit on main. If a future story wants callers (templates, orchestrator prompts) to use `cam issue get` instead of an inline `git show` shell-out, that migration is out of this story's scope.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Official docs don't enumerate exit-code/missing-path behavior explicitly, so verified empirically instead: `git show main:scripts/cam/issues/CAM-9999.json` against the real repo exits 128 with a 'fatal: path ... does not exist in main' stderr message and empty stdout -- confirms getIssueOnMain's `(result.status ?? 1) !== 0` -> { ok: false, reason: 'not-found' } mapping is correct.
